reason: Hyaline cells are the empty, water-storing cells of Sphagnum and Leucobryum leaves.
Plural of hyaline cell.
Hyalocyst is a synonym of hyaline cell in bryophytes.
Leucocyst is a synonym of hyaline cell in Leucobryum and Sphagnum.
The spine-shield is the hardened leaf-base pad that carries the spines (Euphorbia, cacti).
Plural of spine shield.
Style head is the swollen or knobbed apex of the style.
A stigma head is a capitate stigma, not the head of the style. The right target is the stigma (or a stigma shape quality), not this class.
Pistil head is vague. It could mean the stigma, the style apex or the ovary top, so it should not map to style head.
Stylehead is a spelling variant of style head.
Stylar head is a synonym of style head.
Clavuncle is the style head or pollen-presenter of the style apex (Rubiaceae, Apocynaceae).
Clavuncula is the Latin form of clavuncle.
Hyphenated spelling of style head.
A pseudostaminode is a sterile, staminode-like structure in the androecium.
Plural of pseudostaminode.
Interstaminal appendages are any appendages between the stamens. They include corona parts, filament appendages and staminodes, so they are not always pseudostaminodes.
The column foot is the basal extension of the orchid column.
Phrase form of column foot.
The gynostemium is the orchid column, so this is the column foot.
French for foot of the column.
Hyphenated spelling of column foot.
Infrastaminal scales are scales below the stamens, for example in the Apocynaceae corona.
Plural of infrastaminal scale.
Corolla scales include fornices, throat scales and corona scales, not only scales below the stamens.
The articles of a loment-type pod (Desmodium and relatives) are its segments.
A loment article is a loment segment.
A pod segment is a segment of a jointed pod.
The joint of a pod is a segment of a jointed pod.
Fruit article also describes schizocarp parts, such as Brassicaceae lomentaceous fruits and Apiaceae mericarps, which are not loment segments. It would fit only for legume pods.
Fruit segment often means a citrus or other locule segment, or a mericarp. It is not a loment segment.
Trap also names the traps of Nepenthes, Dionaea, Genlisea, Sarracenia and Aldrovanda, not only bladders. It fits only for Utricularia and related bladderworts.
Plural of trap, with the same problem: it covers non-bladder traps.
Buttress in botanical descriptions means the flared base of the trunk, which is formed from roots.
Plank buttresses are a type of buttress root.
Plural of buttress.
French for buttress.
Plural of contrefort.
The perichaetium is the cluster of leaves surrounding the archegonia in bryophytes.
Plural of perichaetium.
French term for perichaetium.
A phyllopodium is the leaf-bearing base on a stem or branch.
Plural of phyllopodium.
Phyllopod is a variant of phyllopodium.
Plural of phyllopod.
Supra-alar cells are the leaf cells above the alar region in mosses.
Plural of supra-alar cell.
Cells of the supra-alar region are supra-alar cells.
The contraligule is the outer ligule on the opposite side of the sheath in grasses and sedges.
Hyphenated spelling of contraligule.
